_comment: BMW F10 coding definitions. The ecuMap blocks describe HOW each value is encoded into a module coding byte (DID, byte offset, bit mask, value map). They are ILLUSTRATIVE and marked verified:false — the app writes them freely in demo mode but refuses to push an unverified map to real hardware. See README (How to add new coding entries) to supply verified maps.

modules.name: FRM
modules.description: Controls all exterior and interior lighting: headlights, fog lights, DRLs, welcome/farewell sequences, and ambient cabin lighting.

modules.name: KOMBI
modules.description: Manages the gauge cluster display, needle sweep animations, digital readouts, and driver information screens.

modules.name: NBT
modules.description: Controls the iDrive infotainment system, navigation display, video playback rules, and connected device behavior.

modules.name: HUD
modules.description: Configures the windshield-projected display including speed units, navigation prompts, and brightness.

modules.name: CAS
modules.description: Manages key fob functions, door lock behavior, and comfort access features.

modules.name: DME
modules.description: The engine control unit. Source of most live engine data (RPM, temperatures, load) and engine-related fault codes. Diagnostics-only in this app — engine coding is out of scope.

codings.name: Cornering Lights
codings.description: Uses the front fog lights as cornering lights when turning at low speed.
codings.longDescription: When enabled, the front fog light on the side you are turning toward will activate as a supplemental cornering light whenever you make a slow turn (under 40 km/h) or engage the parking sensors at low speed. This dramatically improves visibility in dark car parks and tight corners. The fog lights must be physically installed for this feature to work.

codings.name: DRL Brightness
codings.description: Sets the daytime running light brightness as a percentage of maximum output.
codings.longDescription: Controls how bright the daytime running lights (DRLs) appear during daylight driving. The factory default is 70%, but many owners prefer 100% for maximum visibility on motorways, or a lower value like 50% for a subtler, less aggressive look. Changes take effect after the next engine start. Values below 30% may not meet legal DRL requirements in some countries.

codings.name: Welcome Lights Duration
codings.description: How many seconds the exterior lights illuminate when you remotely unlock the car.
codings.longDescription: When you press unlock on the key fob, the exterior lights turn on to guide you to the car in the dark. This setting controls how long that welcome sequence lasts. Set to 0 to disable the welcome sequence entirely if you find it unnecessary or annoying in urban environments where street lighting is sufficient.

codings.name: Ambient Lighting Color
codings.description: Sets the color of the interior ambient lighting strips in the door panels and footwells.
codings.longDescription: The F10 5 Series has ambient LED strips in the door panels and footwells. This coding selects the base color profile. The 'Ice Blue' option matches BMW's factory tone. Actual color rendering depends on the LED hardware installed — cars with single-color strips will show all options as the same color. RGB ambient lighting retrofits can use any of these profiles.

codings.name: Farewell Animation
codings.description: Plays a light fade-out sequence after you lock the car and walk away.
codings.longDescription: After locking the car, the exterior lights play a brief 3-second fade-out animation rather than switching off instantly. This gives the car a premium feel and provides a visual confirmation that locking was successful. Disable this if you park in environments where a brief light flash might be unwanted.

codings.name: Driver-Only First Unlock
codings.description: First key fob press unlocks only the driver door; a second press unlocks all doors.
codings.longDescription: By default, one press on the unlock button opens all four doors at once. With this coding enabled, the first press unlocks only the driver door. A second press within a few seconds unlocks the remaining doors. This is a security preference — it prevents passengers or strangers from opening the car while you are still approaching it in a crowded area.

codings.name: Startup Gauge Sweep
codings.description: Sweeps all instrument cluster needles to maximum and back when you start the engine.
codings.longDescription: When you turn on the ignition, all analog needles (speedometer, tachometer, fuel, temperature) sweep dramatically to their maximum positions and return to zero before settling on their real readings. This is called 'needle staging' and is purely cosmetic. The animation lasts about 2 seconds. It can be disabled if you prefer a more functional, no-frills startup.

codings.name: Digital Speedometer
codings.description: Shows your exact current speed as a large number in the cluster info display.
codings.longDescription: Activates a digital speedometer in the central information area of the instrument cluster, showing your speed as a precise number. This supplements the analog needle — it does not replace it. Useful for accurate speed awareness on motorways or in areas with strict speed cameras, where knowing your precise speed to within 1 km/h matters.

codings.name: Oil Temperature Gauge
codings.description: Activates the blank gauge slot as a live oil temperature readout.
codings.longDescription: The F10 has a gauge housing in the instrument cluster that is left blank on many trim levels from the factory. This coding repurposes it as an oil temperature gauge using data directly from the engine management system. Knowing oil temperature is important if you enjoy spirited driving — you should ideally wait until the oil reaches 80°C before driving hard.

codings.name: Speedometer Unit
codings.description: Switches all speed displays in the cluster between km/h and mph.
codings.longDescription: Changes the primary unit shown on the analog speedometer dial and all digital speed displays in the cluster. If you have imported a car from a country with different speed conventions, or have relocated, this coding lets you switch units without any hardware changes. The change also affects the cruise control speed display and, if equipped, the Head-Up Display.

codings.name: Lap Timer
codings.description: Unlocks a lap timer function in the cluster accessible via the steering wheel buttons.
codings.longDescription: Activates a lap timer that can be started and stopped using the multifunction steering wheel buttons. Elapsed time and sector information are displayed in the cluster info area. This feature is normally restricted to M Performance models, but can be unlocked on standard F10s through coding. It has no effect on vehicle performance or safety systems.

codings.name: Startup Chime
codings.description: Plays the BMW welcome chime through the audio system when the ignition is turned on.
codings.longDescription: Enables the classic BMW welcome gong that plays through the vehicle's audio system immediately after you start the car. This is a premium touch that some configurations ship without, particularly after stereo retrofits. If you find the sound intrusive when starting the car in quiet places (early mornings, car parks), you can disable it here.

codings.name: Video in Motion
codings.description: Removes the lock that prevents video playback on the iDrive screen while driving.
codings.longDescription: By factory default, the iDrive system blocks all video playback (DVD, digital TV, mirrored content) whenever the car is in motion. Enabling this coding removes that restriction. This feature is intended for rear-seat passengers only. It is illegal and dangerous for the driver to watch video while operating a vehicle. Only enable this if you have passengers who wish to use the screen on long journeys.
codings.warning: This disables BMW's safety restriction on in-motion video. Intended for rear passengers only. The driver watching video while driving is illegal in most jurisdictions.

codings.name: Speed Limit Display
codings.description: Shows the current road's posted speed limit in the instrument cluster and/or HUD.
codings.longDescription: When active, the navigation system reads speed limit data from its map database and displays the posted limit directly in the instrument cluster or Head-Up Display. This is a passive awareness tool — it does not intervene in vehicle operation. Accuracy depends on map data being current; limits may lag in construction zones or recently changed roads.

codings.name: Ambient Lighting iDrive Menu
codings.description: Reveals the ambient lighting control submenu in the iDrive Settings.
codings.longDescription: Adds an 'Ambient Lighting' submenu to the iDrive Settings pages, allowing brightness and color adjustments directly from the touchscreen. Without this coding, the menu may be hidden even on cars that have ambient lighting hardware installed. Once revealed, you no longer need a coding tool to change the ambient lighting level day-to-day.

codings.name: Sport Display
codings.description: Adds a performance monitoring page to iDrive showing g-force, throttle, brake, and gear data.
codings.longDescription: Unlocks an additional iDrive page called 'Sport Display' showing real-time lateral and longitudinal g-force, throttle pedal position, brake pressure, and current gear. Data is sourced from the DSC (stability control) module and engine ECU — no additional hardware is required. This is a popular addition for track day preparation or simply for showing off.

codings.name: Screen Auto-Off Timer
codings.description: Minutes of inactivity before the iDrive screen automatically dims to black.
codings.longDescription: Sets how many minutes of complete iDrive inactivity (no touch input, no knob input, no incoming call or notification) must pass before the screen automatically turns off. Set to 0 to never auto-off. Reducing screen-on time can help prolong the display's backlight life over years of ownership and reduces light distraction on motorway cruises.

codings.name: HUD Speed Unit
codings.description: Sets whether the Head-Up Display shows speed in km/h or mph.
codings.longDescription: Controls the speed unit shown in the windshield Head-Up Display projection. This setting is independent from the cluster unit setting — you can display km/h in the cluster and mph in the HUD, or keep them in sync. Most drivers will want both set to the same unit. Changes take effect immediately.

codings.name: Navigation Arrows in HUD
codings.description: Displays turn-by-turn navigation arrows and street names in the Head-Up Display.
codings.longDescription: When active navigation guidance is running, the next turn arrow and street name are projected directly onto the windshield via the HUD. This eliminates the need to glance down at the cluster or iDrive screen for navigation prompts, keeping your focus closer to the road ahead. Requires an active navigation destination to be set in iDrive.

codings.name: HUD Default Brightness
codings.description: The starting brightness level of the HUD projection each time you enter the car.
codings.longDescription: The HUD brightness can be adjusted manually via the instrument cluster controls, but this coding sets the default level restored each time you get into the car. Higher values are better for bright daytime driving when the projection must compete with sunlight; lower values are less distracting at night. Level 5 is a good all-day compromise for most climates.

codings.name: HUD Speed Warning
codings.description: Flashes a warning in the HUD if you exceed this speed. Set to 0 to disable.
codings.longDescription: Configures an optional speed warning overlay in the HUD. If your speed exceeds the threshold set here, the speed readout in the HUD will flash periodically as a visual alert. Set to 0 to disable the warning entirely. A value of 130 is useful for German motorway trips where you want a reminder near the advisory limit.

codings.name: Auto Door Lock Speed
codings.description: All doors automatically lock when the car reaches this speed. Set to 0 to disable.
codings.longDescription: When you exceed the configured speed, all four doors lock automatically as a passive security measure. BMW's factory default is 15 km/h. Many owners increase this to 30 km/h to avoid premature locking while maneuvering in car parks, or disable it entirely (set to 0) if they find it triggers unexpectedly.

codings.name: Remote Window Operation
codings.description: Hold the lock or unlock button on the key fob to close or open all windows.
codings.longDescription: With this coding enabled, holding down the lock button on the key fob for 3 seconds closes all windows (and the sunroof if equipped). Holding the unlock button opens them. This is useful if you forgot to close a window before leaving the car, or want to ventilate the interior on a hot day before getting in. The car must be stationary and locked.

codings.name: Comfort Access Touch Unlock
codings.description: Unlock the car by touching the door handle while the key is in your pocket.
codings.longDescription: Comfort Access is BMW's passive keyless entry system. When enabled, you can unlock the car simply by touching (or gripping) the exterior door handle while the key fob is anywhere within about 1.5 metres — in your bag, jacket pocket, or backpack. You never need to take the key out. The Comfort Access hardware (antennas in the door handles) must be physically installed for this to work.

codings.name: Horn Confirmation on Lock
codings.description: Beeps the horn once to confirm the car locked successfully.
codings.longDescription: When enabled, the car gives a single short horn beep every time it locks via the key fob. This is an audible confirmation that locking succeeded, which is useful in noisy car parks where you might not see the hazard light flash. Disable this if you live in an area where a horn beep is disruptive to neighbors or in quiet early-morning parking situations.

codings.name: Auto Re-Lock Timer
codings.description: If you unlock the car but do not open a door, it re-locks itself after this many seconds.
codings.longDescription: If you remotely unlock the car (for example, from across a car park) but then fail to open any door within the configured time, the car will automatically lock itself again. This protects against accidentally pressing the key fob in your pocket leaving the car unlocked. Set to 0 to disable automatic re-locking if you find it interrupts loading shopping into the boot.
